name: Earth
blurb: Satellite colour imagery (with or without clouds, and night lights), ETOPO1 relief, and the EIGEN-6C4 gravity field and geoid gridded by Fatiando a Terra.

grids.label: Topography
grids.note: ETOPO1 land and sea-floor relief above mean sea level. Ocean depths are shown in blues.

grids.label: Gravity disturbance
grids.note: EIGEN-6C4 gravity at 10 km altitude minus WGS84 normal gravity. Highs over volcanic islands and mountains, lows over deep-sea trenches and old ice-sheet basins.

grids.label: Geoid
grids.note: Geoid height above the WGS84 ellipsoid (EIGEN-6C4). The −106 m low south of India and the +85 m high near New Guinea are the extremes.

images.label: Visible colour
images.note: Cloud-free colour map of Earth from satellite imagery (the "Mappamondo" mosaic, improved with Natural Earth II by Tom Patterson), as prepared for Celestia.

images.label: Visible colour with clouds
images.note: The colour map with a global cloud cover from NASA's Blue Marble Next Generation (a single typical day, not today's weather).

images.label: Night lights
images.note: City lights at night, from NASA Blue Marble and Earth Observatory imagery, as prepared for Celestia.

sites.name: Kennedy Space Center / Cape Canaveral
sites.note: Apollo, Shuttle, Falcon and Artemis launches.

sites.name: Baikonur Cosmodrome
sites.note: Sputnik 1 and Gagarin launched here; still flies Soyuz crews.

sites.name: Guiana Space Centre
sites.note: Ariane and Vega; 5° from the equator.

sites.name: Wenchang
sites.note: Long March 5 and the Chang’e and Tianwen missions.

sites.name: Apollo 11 splashdown
sites.note: Pacific Ocean, recovered by USS Hornet.

sites.name: Soyuz landing zone
sites.note: Kazakh steppe near Dzhezkazgan; Gagarin landed near Engels, Russia.
